title: MDA / IMS-MDA / MIDAS
reason: scope:IMS-MDA: The poster explicitly groups IMS-MDA with MDA and expands its name as immunomagnetic separation for targeted bacterial enrichment for MDA. The Seth-Smith abstract specifically establishes targeted bacterial enrichment followed by MDA whole-genome amplification and sequencing. With the drawn shared MDA component, this supports o_hybridize and the two Phi 29 synthesis stages at schematic level. Enrichment is context upstream of the drawn Genome input, not an invented bead-handling operation in this graph; enrichment does not certify perfect target purity. Exact applicability of the terminal o_s1 to the Seth-Smith IMS-MDA implementation remains unresolved: neither a separate IMS branch nor its finishing chemistry is given in the available abstract. The S1 route is retained at grouped-family level, without assigning its post-S1 output history to IMS-MDA as an experimentally verified step. Resolving that member-specific terminal claim would require the relevant full-text protocol passage or an explicit source mapping.

candidate.title: MDA / IMS-MDA / MIDAS
candidate.scope: Grouped molecular amplification schematic for MDA (multiple displacement amplification), IMS-MDA (immunomagnetic separation for targeted bacterial enrichment followed by MDA), and MIDAS (microwell displacement amplification system), at the implementation detail actually drawn in the assigned poster row. Inventory: Genome → Hybridize primers under “3′ blocked random hexamer primers” → first Phi 29 / Synthesis with “Nascent replication fork” → second Phi 29 / Synthesis with increased branching → S1 nuclease → Amplified DNA. This is one shared biochemical route, not three separate drawn branches or a pooling operation. Phi 29 and S1 nuclease are enzyme annotations on transformations; the nascent fork is a structural annotation. The short primer end marks are visible but do not establish a chemical structure. The adjacent smMIP, MIPSTR and MALBAC workflows and right-hand chemical structures are outside this assigned row. Only these three named targets are extracted: the broader collection page also discusses ddMDA and SNES, which are not target alternatives in this schematic. Primary evidence qualifies the shared depiction: IMS enrichment and MIDAS compartment handling are unshown contexts; the primer-end wording is interpreted using extendable random primers; and the documented MIDAS conversion to unbranched DNA uses DNA polymerase I and Ampligase rather than the drawn S1 route. The graph preserves the S1 route as drawn, with per-member applicability below. Its endpoint is amplified genomic DNA, preceding any unshown library construction, sequencing or data analysis. It does not claim complete implementation identity or interchangeability among the grouped methods.

states.label: Genome

No physical topology, complete chromosome structure, cell, bead, microwell or attachment is encoded by this icon.

For IMS-MDA the named method supplies target-bacterium enrichment before genomic amplification; for MIDAS the primary source places genomic amplification in separate microwells. These contexts are not additional drawn states.

research_questions.question: The poster explicitly groups IMS-MDA with MDA and expands its name as immunomagnetic separation for targeted bacterial enrichment for MDA. The Seth-Smith abstract specifically establishes targeted bacterial enrichment followed by MDA whole-genome amplification and sequencing. With the drawn shared MDA component, this supports o_hybridize and the two Phi 29 synthesis stages at schematic level. Enrichment is context upstream of the drawn Genome input, not an invented bead-handling operation in this graph; enrichment does not certify perfect target purity. Exact applicability of the terminal o_s1 to the Seth-Smith IMS-MDA implementation remains unresolved: neither a separate IMS branch nor its finishing chemistry is given in the available abstract. The S1 route is retained at grouped-family level, without assigning its post-S1 output history to IMS-MDA as an experimentally verified step. Resolving that member-specific terminal claim would require the relevant full-text protocol passage or an explicit source mapping.
